column2: pi-jev-model-router: Jev judges the task, code owns the budget — model routing with daily spend caps pi-jev-model-router v0.2.0: One Jev request with 4 parallel questions before every turn: task_kind (Choice), complexity (Score), capability_deserved (Score), needs_deep_reasoning (Noul). Then: demand = 0.55*complexity + 0.45*capability (+ reasoning nudge); demand = max(demand, kind floor) # planning

browser-use/jev-ultrafast: dynamic action space for browser agents, clicks never touch an LLM browser-use/jev-ultrafast: indexing the live page into a dynamic action space, then asking Jev to pick both the operation and the target element. A small LLM is invoked only for TYPE_TEXT operations. Everything else — click, scroll, select — never touches a generative model.

aidxn: cheap models as always-on watchers — the expensive model thinks, the cheap model stares aidxn.com — cheap models as always-on watchers: "The expensive model does the thinking, the cheap model does the staring." tail -f dev.log | grep -Ei 'error|failed', then a small model reads the matches and answers one question: did anything actually explode. A Haiku-class model does it perfectly

Maximem: a map of decision seams — where NOT to put a classifier in an agent Maximem — a map of decision seams: "can you write down every possible answer before seeing the input, and does code do something different for each one? If the answer is a sentence, it is not a seam." Warns most disappointment comes from pointing Jev at whole use cases instead of individual seams.
